Shen Wei is a twenty-two-year-old orphan working as a junior lab technician at Clearsky Pharmaceuticals in Yongcheng, the a megacity of Tianji—a modern cultivation world where spiritual energy has been industrialized and nearly depleted. With Grade C spiritual roots and a cultivation stuck at Qi Condensation Stage 3 for over two years, he has no realistic path to advancement. His only distinction is an unusually deep knowledge of cultivation theory, which he studies obsessively despite having no means to apply it.

During a routine late-shift inventory of old project materials, Shen Wei discovers a jade pendant classified as an inert artifact. Despite showing no response to instruments, the pendant is warm to his touch and reacts faintly when he channels Qi into it. He pockets it. Unbeknownst to him, that single action will change the course of his life.

There are no Sects. There are no Elders. There are no Systems. There are no Cheats. 

I've read three hundred cultivation novels. I know exactly how this is supposed to go — find a cave, discover an ancient manual, join a sect, climb the ranks, avoid dangerous jade beauties, and punch a god.

None of that exists here.

Sects haven't been built yet.

I wasn't lucky enough to be given a snarky System to track my progression. 

I wasn't given a golden finger to bypass my lack of talent.

I instead, was transmigrated into a fifteen-year-old farmer's body in a world where cultivation is unregulated and nobody has figured out how to master it, let alone teach it. 

I'm in a world full of warlords conscripting farmers into meat grinders and cultivators operating like weapons of mass destruction.

Yea, this isn't the transmigration I was hoping for. I need to throw all the tropes I've read out of the window, because I am in a predicament that no one else has ever been in before.

But on the bright side, I can now introduce some Common Sense into this world. 

What to expect:

◈ Rational, strategic male MC — no power fantasies, no plot armor, every advantage earned
◈ Pre-sect xianxia worldbuilding — cultivation exists, institutions don't, the MC builds them from scratch
◈ Kingdom building / clan building / sect founding — village to settlement to sect progression
◈ Progression fantasy with real costs — every gain is paid for, every system is tested
◈ Cozy village life meets warring states tension
◈ 2,000-3,000 word chapters
◈ Daily updates, three-chapter bonus drops on milestone days
◈ This is a long-form serial — settle in

What is better: to enter the multiverse gifted with power, or to begin weak and claw your way to strength through blood, will, and relentless effort?

When Earth is integrated into the Multiverse, humanity gains stats, skills, and magic—but only a select few are granted System Cores, becoming Core-bearers with a clear path to power.

Cade Whitehollow, a burned-out, indebted postdoc who has just been fired, is not one of them. Even so, he refuses to let this second life collapse into the same dead end as the first.

With no Core, no Class, and no head start, Cade is thrown into a lethal Tutorial designed for Core-bearers.

While they level, cast spells, and surge ahead, Cade has to survive the long, brutal grind of becoming eligible to forge a Core of his own.

Monsters evolve. Humans turn on each other. And buried somewhere in the chaos of the Tutorial is an ancient path to power—one even the System cannot control.

For Ethan, the answer comes easily.

Earth has been pulled into the vast multiverse trial, one where survival isn’t guaranteed and failure means extinction. Humanity is scattered across dangerous levels, each one more brutal than the last, racing against time to clear them before everything collapses.

Ethan has seen how it ends.

Until he’s given a chance.

Would you like to restart?

It’s time to do it again. Time to pick up the mantle and become the Knight humanity needs.

I wanted nothing more than an ordinary life—free from crushing debt and the endless corporate grind.
Instead, I died. And when I opened my eyes, I was in ancient Rome.

My father? Gaius Julius Caesar—the man destined to rule, or ruin, the Republic.

But history is written in blood. If I do nothing, my new family will be swept away by the coming political firestorm.
Power is survival in Rome, and I intend to survive.

Armed with modern knowledge, I will reshape the Roman Republic—through banking, insurance, industry, and new political strategies.

Rome will never be the same.

What happens when a young master from a declining cultivator clan decides to… be a decent human being?

Zhao Ren was not a typical young master. No arrogance, no entourage, no random face‑slapping, at least not any more. He preferred to read books over throwing his weight around. Raised to turn around his family's fortunes, he struggles to live up to their lofty ideals. But man plans and the heavens laugh. Instead he found his own way to the Dao. 

A cultivator who likes a sustainable approach to growing herbs and leaves behind inheritances instead of looting everything not nailed down? Who even spares a thought for those who come after?

Who does that?

Why would you refine a precious pill and not swallow it immediately? Why would you craft spirit weapons with your hard earned, expensive ingredients without ever intending to use or sell them? Why even bother planting a tree that won’t bear fruit until long after you’re dead?

This guy must be crazy! So how does he keep getting stronger?!

What to expect:

-Mass release initially then 1 chapter a day M-W-F. 

- ~2k words per chapter (Slightly longer first chapter)

-Slightly more farming, crafting and slice-of-life than most xianxias

-MC doesn't discover his own path until Ch 10 so be patient

-Gradually accumulating power growth.

-No Harem

Lord Dread was the first lich in history, and the greatest magical prodigy the world has ever seen. The Gods themselves feared his potential, and they banished him for it. They should have been more thorough.

After freeing himself from his prison of countless millennia, Lord Dread finds that his powers have been diminished, and that his body is now that of a baby girl. Born to an aristocratic family, and with a fresh chance to begin re-learning magic in a better way than he taught himself originally, his sights are soon set on regaining his former glory. He must learn about this strange new time period he's found himself in, rebuild the dark empire that he once used to challenge even the Gods, and then, finally, take revenge on the fearful divinity that saw fit to strike him down in the past.

This would be easier, if girls could inherit land, but Lord Dread has never been one to let a little something like that get in his way.

STAFF NOTE: The author had proven ownership. RighteousEgg is the original author. I have added a pinned comment to the first chapter to show this staff note is legitimate.


Su Chen died. That was when the real cheat code finally activated. A mysterious ancient tome called the Reverse Fate Scripture latched onto his soul. Every time he dies, it coldly tallies his previous life's feats, failures, and sheer audacity—then awards Reverse Fate Points. 

Spend them wisely: perfect-grade talent, heaven-defying comprehension, god-tier bloodlines, imperial birthrights, demonic heritages… anything to rewrite the script of the next existence. And so the cycle begins.

He's been the arrogant trash young master, discarded by his own clan like yesterday's garbage.

He's been the iron-blooded general who never lost a battle… until the battlefield claimed him.

He's worn the crown as emperor, ruled the world with an iron fist—only to be killed by the very family he trusted.

He's been the sect's unrivaled senior brother, sword in hand, crushing every genius in his generation.

He's been a demonic cultivator who bathed righteous sects in blood.

He's even become a devouring Nether Raven, swallowing entire worlds… 

Lifetime after lifetime.

Failure. Betrayal. Glory. Catastrophic falls.

Every death just feeds the next run—making him sharper, stronger, more ruthless.

Now, armed with memories from countless lives, battle-hardened experience, and a terrifying mountain of hoarded Reverse Fate Points, he opens his eyes once more.

This time, he's nobody's pawn. He's engineering the single most broken starting build imaginable. Everything that ever crushed him underfoot is getting stomped right back—hard.

From worm to apex predator. From crippled trash to untouchable sovereign. From mortal speck to standing above the heavens themselves. Countless openings. Countless brutal deaths. All converging on one inevitable endgame—To reach the pinnacle of every cycle and shatter this cursed fate once and for all!

His family was his world. Now he’s in a new one.

When a fatal accident rips Caleb Foster from his wife and kids, the forty-year-old gets a second chance in a realm of dungeons and monsters. A cosmic system offers him a choice of legendary powers, but Caleb refuses the flashy magic. He chooses the abilities to learn faster, remember perfectly, and master any physical skill.

A father's instinct to protect doesn't die with his family. To survive and shield the new lives that depend on him, he must use a lifetime of quiet competence to navigate a dangerous frontier town, hunt deadly beasts, and outwit men who mistake his lack of flash for weakness.

In a place where might makes right, Caleb is about to show that the most lethal weapon is a mind that misses nothing, and a will that never quits.

***

I died and woke up in a soldier’s body. 

We’re Duplicates. Dupes. An artificial army built from a template, born with access to the System and a [Soldier] class. And we’re the kingdom’s only hope for surviving the orc hordes. 

Dupes have enormous potential, but sometimes, the souls of people from other worlds can transmigrate into their bodies. That was where I came in—I was just a college student from Earth, wasting away in a degree I didn’t care about, but now, I’m an Atoning, serving on the front lines to pay off my “theft of soul.”

Here, survival is a luxury. We’re nothing but fodder for a crumbling empire. I’m up against orcs, mutated monsters, and disgruntled members of my battalion who want to put a knife in my soul-stealing back. But there’s a chance, no matter how slim, to become more than just a soldier and turn my name into a legend. 

If I can’t rise above the rot that’s taken hold of this world, no one else will. 

This is a skill-merging Litrpg for people who like a little more thoughtful progression and stories that are lighter on the Litrpg elements. 

What to expect:

- Military litrpg

- A hopeful MC in a gritty world, building ragtag teams and helping out where he can

- Daily chapters

He died a nobody.
Now he’s reborn in a body beaten and left for dead, no family, no food, no future.

In the Kingdom of Avalon, strength isn’t just respected, it’s survival. Power is ranked by Tiers, magic is earned through blood and elemental affinity, and those without talent are nothing more than fodder for war.

Edward has neither noble blood nor rare talent. What he does have is an iron will, a sharp mind, and the stubborn refusal to stay down. Desperate for food, shelter, and a second chance, he enlists in the Royal Army, trading the uncertainty of the streets for the grueling discipline of military life.

But the army is no place for the weak. Training is brutal, resources are scarce, and every recruit is just one mistake away from the grave. Here, camaraderie is forged in hardship, tactics matter as much as raw strength, and survival demands more than swinging a sword, it demands learning, adapting, and enduring.

The road ahead is long and unforgiving. Yet with each step, Edward edges closer to something greater, growth, purpose, and perhaps a place in a kingdom that would rather see him buried than crowned.

Rise… or be forgotten.

What to expect:

  ~Slow-paced progression

  ~Non-OP

  ~Military focus

  ~Gritty, grounded tone

  ~No harem

  ~Detailed worldbuilding

  ~Coming-of-age journey

  ~Kingdom building (later in the story)

Sorin was already a legend in his own time. He thought his journey was complete, but it’s only just begun.

It is said that those who reach the top of the tower become immortal. After forty years of calculated risks, dead companions, and spent fortunes, Sorin Atharel was ready to take the final step and join those hallowed ranks. Instead, his reward was to have his soul space stripped bare, all his abilities ripped away, and his anima drained to nothing.

He wakes in the bottom floor of a tower, but not his tower. Surrounded by strangers in a strange city, he quickly realizes the truth. Far from becoming immortal, his whole life has been reset. With only the clue of an intricate tile mosaic depicting his first life adorning the floor of his soul space, he must navigate his new reality. If he wants answers to what was done to him, there’s only one way to get strong enough to find them: he must climb again.

Alric wakes up in another world with all the usual assumptions already in place: a sword, a system menu, and the quiet expectation that he’ll start acting like a hero.

He doesn’t.

Instead, he starts paying attention.

Coins circulate too long to make sense. Measurements are imprecise. Beer is sour, but everyone drinks it anyway. Magic exists, but no one can explain why it works when it does, because it usually works well enough.

As Alric tries to find his footing, he brings with him habits from a more systematic world: watching how things are done, tracking what’s missing, and assuming that inconsistencies point to underlying rules.

Sometimes they do.
Sometimes they reveal reasons things were never “fixed” in the first place.

This is a slow-burn isekai about logistics, brewing, and learning what happens when methodical thinking collides with a society that functions, imperfectly, on its own terms.

Progress is possible.
Improvement is not always welcome.

What to expect:
Slow burn observation with show rather than tell. 
A methodical, craft-focused fantasy about brewing, trade, and the consequences of practical innovation.
A blend between cozy slice-of-life and small business starting up in a new ecoscape.
This is a methodical progression story rather than a combat-focused one.
Less dungeon crawling. More ledgers, fermentation, and the occasional economic incident

Chen Yang died once.

He was reborn as a helpless infant in a new world, one ruled not by sciences, but by cultivation, where enlightenment shapes reality, and the Dao governs all things.

At first, Chen Yang believes this world is merely unfamiliar. Only later does he realize the truth: his death and rebirth have awakened a strange ability, one that allows him to travel between worlds. Not as a conqueror. Not as a hero. But as an observer, a learner, and eventually, a cultivator of understanding.

Unaware of the greater forces watching him, Chen Yang chooses a path rarely walked. Rather than chasing power through violence, he becomes a scholar first, studying the Dao through cultivation, crafting, and quiet contemplation. Every realm he visits offers new truths, new materials, and new perspectives, each shaping his growing comprehension of existence itself.

This is not a tale of quick ascension or endless battles. Power is earned slowly. Every cultivation realm is explored in detail. Crafting is methodical. Enlightenment comes through patience, failure, and insight.

Chen Yang's journey is not toward domination, but toward knowing.

And the Dao is endless.

Updates from Monday to Fridays

-  A nice sect without backstabbing

- Weak to strong MC

- Slow, deliberate cultivation progression

- Detailed cultivation realms and Daoist philosophy

- Crafting-focused growth and experimentation

- World hopping with deep exploration of each realm

- Minimal combat, no harem, no romance

- Scholar-style MC focused on understanding over conquest

- Minor LitRPG elements

- Slow paced - slice of life

LitRPG kingdom builder. Cultivation world.

After meeting Truck-kun, Benton, a grandfather and an overall nice man, is transmigrated into the body of Chao Su in a brutal, might-makes-right cultivation world.

Things could be worse. He is given choices that come with neat advantages, and his career in middle management gives him ample experience leading people. Those skills should translate to running a sect.

Unfortunately, things aren't that simple. Benton quickly realizes that his plan to let his recruits fight for him won't work. He'll need to get up to speed on life in a cultivation world fast because danger is on the way. A beast tide threatens his new territory. Rival sects don't like the balance of power being upset. Worse, the demonic cultivators that destroyed Chao Su's prior sect are still out there.

A/N - Apologies, but I do not do shoutout swaps.

What to Expect:

- This is not a cultivation story. The MC cannot cultivate and advances through cultivation realms by earning points from the System.

- No artificial emphasis.

- The MC makes decisions based on empathy and emotions, treating his sect members like he's their doting grandfather. He's not a typical Xianxia protagonist.

- The story isn't exactly cozy, but it's on the lower end as far as tension goes. If a rating of 1 is no tension at all and 10 is drop the protagonist from the frying pan into the fire, rinse, repeat, the readers agree that this story is about a 4.

- No sexual content or a harem.

- M-W-F-Sa-Su with occasional bonus chapters

- Average Chapter Length = Approximately 2,000 Words

- MC goes from weak to strong to OP.

- Though the story is not a comedy, the tone is mostly light, and it contains humorous elements.

- There is some romance between side characters. There are no current plans for the MC to have a love interest. Just to be clear (and I'm only mentioning this because it's the internet and ... people), there is absolutely no possibility that the sixty-year-old isekai'd protagonist will develop a romantic relationship with any of his teenage disciples. He views them as his grandkids.

- Minor swearing occasionally.

All Ryan ever wanted to do was become an adventurer.

Quests, skills, quirky teammates and posting exploits on Realmnet. What’s not to love?

Instead he’s broke, working at a Manaburger, and System slots cost more than his paycheck times ten thousand.

Then he gets shot.
Then the Trial System chooses him.
Then he ends up in a Trial, with hostile Earth soldiers—from his own country no less.

Ryan just wanted to play adventurer. Instead, he’s fighting with every authority figure, stabbing a sword prodigy in a deathmatch, and… immediately getting blacklisted from the Adventurer’s Guild?

Suddenly Ryan's no longer just a fry cook. He's a rare Destined, tasked with figuring out how to save not one, but two worlds. It just doesn't seem that way to anyone else.

But hey, in a world ruled by Tyrants, what’s a villain but a hero adventurer with an attitude?

What to expect:

+ Ryan is a lovable [Rogue]. Weak to strong to op.

+ A post-integration world(s) where things have settled, but conflict is starting to bubble under the surface.

+ Power and choice, choice and power. Progression in both skills and character.

+ arrogant mages, intelligent monsters, guns, drones, selfies, [Meteors], covens, cults, shitposting epigraphs and a Gamielle.

+ A Witch Tyrant who will hex people through the internet for very mean comments.

+ No harem.

--

Updates everyday (2.5k-3.5k chapters) while we're on rising stars! Then we'll go back to 5 a day schedule with [BEGONE CLIFF] for extra chapters (Check out chapter 27 author's notes).

Long time reader, first time storyteller. I've been working on Ryan's tale for a while now and it's finally at the stage where I'm proud to share it. There's a lot of inspirations here. From system apocalypses to world hopping to cultivation and just plain epic fantasy. You'll find elements of all of them here, blended into something that I believe is fairly unique.

“If this is a story worth saving, then mediocrity has truly won.” — Celestia von Reingarde

* * * * *

After one late-night drive ended my life, I woke inside the very first webnovel I mocked.

In the pages of Tower of the End, Celestia von Reingarde was nothing more than a petty villainess, a spoiled noble girl with sharp eyes and crimson pupils, remembered only for bullying someone until the “hero,” Arthur, arrived to play the gentleman. One humiliation, and she faded away so the harem could bloom.

Except now, I had become Celestia.

At first, I thought I could slip away. Why should I meddle with Arthur’s destined rise? Let him climb the tower, collect his lovers, and save the world. I could just live quietly in the background. But the world disagreed.

A voice seared through my mind:

[Warning! Story Relevance: 3/100.]
[Warning! Existence will be erased when Story Relevance reaches 0/100.]

Now, obscurity meant death.

In their quest to reach the pinnacle of cultivation, geniuses forge their path with the belief that the path of slaughter is the only one that can lead them there. But for some strange reason, they always encounter hidden masters who, without ever having left their sects or fought physically, surpass them in cultivation, having reached higher realms than their own.

The protagonist of this story, an archaeologist specializing in dead languages, dies after finding a door that should not have existed and is reborn in another world, where, due to a very bad decision she does not remember making, she is denied any possibility of taking the most orthodox and fastest path of slaughter, so she has no choice but to take things slowly and follow the path of all those hidden masters, aided by her former talent for understanding and deciphering various languages.

What to expect:

-Strange as it may seem, this story is a Slice of Life cultivation novel, so things move slowly, don't expect a speed run of cultivation.

-Due to the protagonist's special circumstances, don't expect a lot of combat or fighting. And when there is, because it's still a cultivation world, it will always be brief and not too drawn out.

-The protagonist knows nothing about cultivation and isn't a regular reader of web novels, as is usually the case, so she starts from scratch and has to figure everything out little by little.

-The protagonist doesn't forget her old life or everything she knows about it in the first dozen episodes either, which—combined with the previous point—means she often compares what she discovers and learns in this new world with the things she knows from her old one.

-An attempt to make the characters interesting and with their own personalities. Only time will tell if I succeed or not.

-A unique and original cultivation system, don't expect Qi Realms and Golden Cores.

Additional notices:

-This is the English version translated by a professional AI. Unfortunately, my English is not good enough to write directly in it, so I am adding the AI-generated content label. I am also publishing the original Spanish version.

-I used a translator up until Chapter 55. Starting with chapter 56, I began using a different one, which most readers say is much better.

-I'm also retranslating the first few chapters using the new translator. The chapters that have already been retranslated are marked with an (R) in the title.

-The cover is also AI-generated while I find an artist to create an original one for me.

A post-apocalyptic LitRPG series inspired by The Primal Hunter, Defiance of the Fall, and Elden Ring.

Jacob Cloud is sixteen, a miner’s son, and he knows his fate: die young, broke, and anonymous in the bowels of Shit’s Creek, a nowhere town that feeds silver ore to richer cities and spits out its sons in pine boxes. He dreams of more. In this world, Knights are one step above Adventurers—protectors, guides, and, most importantly, heroes. But to even try for a Knight’s life, you need gold, rare Skills, and connections Jacob will never have.

Then one day, the mine floor gives out. Jacob falls—not to his death, but into the chance of a lifetime: a Rainbow-ranked Skill Crystal, something so rare people kill over them, and so powerful it could turn a nobody into a legend. Except Jacob doesn’t get a weapon or healing Skill. He gets The Grimoire Extraordinaire—a support Skill that doesn’t even attack, defend, or heal. It shows him the flaws in any Skill or item, nothing more. No instant power. No glory.

But Jacob isn’t an idiot. He grinds. He experiments. He uses the Grimoire to fix the basics: how to grip a pick, how to channel mana, how to train. In five days trapped underground, he boosts his mining skills to levels nobles would envy. When he claws his way out, he’s ready to quit the mines for good.

In a modern Korea where 15% of humanity awakens as Manaborn, rifts tear open, spilling monsters; and opportunity. The strong rise as Rifters, earning fame, power, and a chance at a life beyond fear. And those who can't? They get swallowed by the world.

Sam Jimin, a poor orphan scraping by the outskirts of Seoul, never expected much from life. Bullied and ignored, he pinned his hopes on a miracle during his Awakening; anything to escape the bottom.

He didn’t get one.

His official result: Rank E-1. No skills. A dead end.

Fortunately for David, the homestead already has a cabin. Sure, there are squatters, and he’s going to have to adjust to a world with magic and a System, but he’s the only one with a massive 600 horsepower New Holland T9 Quadtrac tractor! 

But even with modern tech in an 1800s otherworld, not everything’s coming up roses. Please read this first:

(21/12/2025) Arc 1 (Books 1 and 2) of Path of the Last Champion should hopefully be published sometime early-ish next year. I highly, highly recommend that if you like the idea of this story, that you wait for that version to come out. It will be a far more epic and pleasurable entry into what I promise is going to be a legendary journey. After taking everyone's feedback and advise into consideration, I've done a full re-write of Arc 1 to address all those issues. So, it would mean the world to me if you read that newer version instead!

That said, if you would like to read the story in its first version, then know that the annoying bits should be self-contained to and resolved by the end of Arc 1! 

Again, thank you all so, so much for all your feedback, comments, and messages! You have, and continue to be, instrumental to the growth of this story!

A sinner rises, a sword becomes legend, an ancient lie unravels…

The Path of the Last Champion begins, and nothing will ever be the same.

Nar was born in darkness, and he was meant to die there – a slave, a sinner, shackled by a sin long ago forgotten and doomed to a life beneath the surface.

His eyes were never meant to see the dazzling lights of the Infinite Nexus, nor the wonders of the Endless Labyrinth from aboard great aetherships. He was never destined for power, a class, or the System… But he made the choice few sinners dare – to Climb.

Now, he must forge a hybrid tank/DPS class, hide a secret that could get him kicked from his Climbing party, and achieve the impossible in order to save his dying father, who sacrificed everything to ensure Nar’s future. He will face everything that lies in wait for him in the darkness of the Between-Nexus, and beyond that, Nar will need to grow strong in a society where might makes right, in order to one day make the journey back for his dad before it's too late…

However, without knowing it, with every step he takes towards the City Without End, Nar is bringing to a close a play that has spanned eternities. The players are all assembling for the final act that will decide the fate of Creation Itself, but no one is expecting Nar… Nor the lengths he is willing to go in order to rescue his dad.

Nar is no chosen one, but he will be the Last Champion.

What to expect:

- A Sci-Fantasy LitRPG with massive world building, realistic party based combat centered around the holy trinity classes (+ party leaders!) with many unique paths/affinities (becoming more relevant in Arc 2!), an advanced tech society, dungeons, huge raids, mysterious plot, epic battles, and more!

- A System that has been established for a long, long time (“There's nothing new in the Nexus!”) and which is crucial for the very functioning of society itself.

- Support characters that will have unique classes/paths, as well as their own growth, motivations and storylines, and who will always remain relevant to the story (there will be different POVs, but MC’s POV is 95% of the story).

- Slow burn and earned power! Nothing is given, there are no handouts, and no shortcuts!

- If you enjoy Star Wars, Final Fantasy, Tower of God, One Piece and others like this, you might like this story too!

- Arc 1 is a Tower Climber through a vast, ancient, uncaring and cruel machine world. Our characters are flawed, and at times dumb, annoying and make poor decisions! But they learn and grow, and by the end of Arc 1, they’ve got themselves mostly put together, and have forged unbreakable bonds!

- Arc 2 is after the Climb, and after the craziness and everything that the party endured in Arc 1, this is their chance to catch a bit of a breather, and learn more of the outside world. But there are secrets in the dark, things in motion our party does not yet suspect, and their break will not last forever...

- Arc 3 arrives like a storm after the end of Arc 2 and is currently releasing! Big changes are coming for Nar and the party as they are thrust into their first long delve. Welcome to the Brightnight domain, the jungle ruled by the night, and a place of monstrous beasts and insane gains! There is no doubt that this will be a perilous delve, but the greatest danger might just come from those to whom you extend a helping hand to... And who knows what secrets lie forgotten in the sweltering jungle?

- 3 chapters weekly (MON-WED-FRI)

- Average 3k words per chapter

Civil engineer Arthur Vance was two days away from marrying the love of his life when a truck ended his future.

Instead of death, he awakens in the body of Oliver Ashborn—a frail thirteen-year-old noble who has just survived an assassination attempt.

His new reality is worse than death.

The once-powerful Ashborn family is collapsing. Their mines are exhausted. Their roads are mud. Their territory is drowning in debt. And powerful enemies are already circling.

But Arthur isn't a noble.
He's an engineer.

Armed with the knowledge of physics, chemistry, and structural engineering, Arthur begins to analyze this new world's greatest force—magic.

If mana follows rules, then it can be understood.
If it can be understood, it can be engineered.
And in a world where magic decides power… one mistake could destroy everything.

=> Updates: 3-5 times per week!

What to expect from this novel:

⚙️ Rational, Engineer Protagonist
🔮 Hard Magic System
📈 Weak-to-Strong Progression
🏰 Kingdom Building & Industrialization
⚔️ Fantasy & Political Intrigue
🗝️ Deep Lore & Mysteries
⏳ Slow Romance

This is my first experience in writing, and I hope to get better with time, and be able to stand on my own.

Tangerine Stone is an S tier trouble magnet with a hate for Tuesdays. Follow along as she joins a magic academy, makes friends with a brain slug, tries to understand her place in this new world, and hopefully flirts with some pretty girls.


What to expect: 

GL, Tangerine is a big old disaster lesbian. All of the horny and no where to put it.

No Harem or poly, Tangerine is a bit of a flirt, but if or when she settles down she is a *slightly* possessive one woman type of girl. 

This isn't really a Litrpg, but it gets kinda close, no stats but lots of collecting magic items.

Tropes, yes! Its a portal adventure where Tangerine is forceable conscripted joins a magic academy, deal with almost Otome situations in a world that is discount MtG!

How MtG? I'm being inspired by the cards but not the lore. There's no Jace hanging about here. I'm also shamelessly bringing in a lot of inspiration from other stuff I like! 

Slice of life, Each update is just another day. There will be some action and adventure hopefully some angst and drama too! Think Buffy the Vampire Slayer for tone.

Weak to strong, kinda. More like unprepared to prepared.

Single character first person focus, 99% of chapters will be from the perspective of Tangerine. I'm not going to say I will never do a different point of view, but it will be rare.

No ai has touched this work, you can tell because of all the mistakes!

Book one Complete!

When thrown into a different world, the typical Isekai protagonist gets some sort of a cheat. Be it an ancient technique, a grandpa stuck inside a ring, a unique system, a rare magical treasure, special bloodline, knowing the future events or heaven defying luck. In Xiao Yun's case all he got was crippled cultivation and a crumbling clan. If one thing sets him apart from the masses, it's his Earthly knowledge and he is forced to put that knowledge into use to try and find a safe spot for himself in this new and absurd reality.

What to expect: Smart MC, Mature MC, Cunning MC, Clan Building, Politics, Lots of Trope Subversion, Hidden Knowledge, Slow Pace, Developed Side Characters, Crippled Cultivation(for real), Strong Female Characters and Slow Progression.

Additional Notes: If you are a long time reader of the Cultivation genre, you might particularly enjoy this novel(If you are new to the genre you will miss many jokes and references and the story itself might be confusing). You will find many references to other cultivation novels and cliches, as well some pop culture references. I deliberately picked certain cliche characters and situations and decided to give them my own personal twist. I'm a fan of the genre and there are plenty of tropes that I find frustrating and can be a turn off for many fans like myself, so I decided to target those tropes and play around with them. Be warned though, I will include even THAT particular cultivation novel trope(the one with the "magic medicine"), the trope that pushes away so many fans of cultivation/xianxia/wuxia genre away due to it's perverse nature, but I will be giving it my own personal twist which will change it's nature and make for a funny interaction . It will be done in the future chapters, as I want to set it up properly so the story is actually coherent. 

Extra Notes: English is not my first language, so if you find any typos and nonsensical sentences, or something that you feel is incoherent, feel free to point them out. I use Word to edit my chapters and fix such things, but as this is my first proper attempt at a novel and I lack the funds for an editor, there might be some mistakes.

They’ve been drinking my future like it’s corp-subsidized coffee. I’m about to make them choke on it.

I’m Dash. My great-grandfather was one of the Fifteen who saved humanity during the System Apocalypse, founding the corps that rule the solar system. That legacy should’ve been mine. Until my father was caught up in corpo politics, disinherited and died, leaving us with nothing but a single building on Earth 2.0.

Then I nearly died, and a broken System manifested—barely functional, stripped down to the bones. But it came with Hoqalo, a tinkerer’s trait that lets me forge gear that punches way above its tier. And the more I dig into why my System came out wrong, the more it looks like someone made sure it would.

Someone with corporate reach. Someone who wanted the Kallum bloodline to stay down. To fight them, I’ve got my hands, my tools, and friends who’ll go to corpo hell and back with me.

They stole my future. Time to steal it back with interest.

Each chapter is ~2,5k–4,5k words!

You can support me on Patreon! Currently ~250 pages ahead: https://www.patreon.com/PlotArmorHQ

What to expect

Cyberpunk LitRPG: Deep system mechanics with a unique twist: A Broken System with glitchy stats and magic!
Sci-Fi x Fantasy: A corporate dystopia (Earth 2.0) where ancient magic and futuristic tech collide.
Hopepunk: This story isn't grimdark. The worldbuilding is still exploiting people, but the tone is not dark, quite the opposite.
The Protagonist: A sarcastic, scrappy underdog heir fighting his way up from the bottom with wit and terrible puns.
Corporate Intrigue: A mystery involving the Sol Fortune 15, family legacies, and secret sabotage.
Slice-of-Life: Exploring the gritty and glamorous reality of life on Earth 2.0.
Slow Burn Romance: Natural chemistry with a twist and relationship building (not the main focus, but present).
No Harem.
